title: Econ Bridge: Field Ops Healthboard & Go/No‑Go Runbook for Batching/Caching/Quantization
creator: Marina Lopez
description:
Goal: Create an operational 'healthboard' and a concise Go/No-Go runbook for rolling out adaptive batching, KV prefix caching, and model quantization profiles to production cohorts. This ticket coordinates the final validation gate across Product, Eng, SRE, and Solutions so cost-saving knobs can be enabled with measurable safety nets and rollback paths.

Scope: 1) Healthboard: one-page dashboard (Console + PagerDuty hook) showing token-unit impact, tail latency percentiles, model correctness regression signal, and cache hit rates per route. 2) Go/No-Go runbook: preflight checks, gating thresholds, canary sizes, automated rollback triggers, manual escalation paths, and stakeholder owners. 3) Field trial scaffold: templates for experiment labeling, metric collection (A/B and holdout), and customer opt-in communications.

Acceptance criteria: - Healthboard populated with production traffic for two representative routes (chat-bot, document-embeddings) and validated against historical baselines. - Runbook includes numeric SLOs and regression thresholds (e.g., +0.5% top1 accuracy drop max, p99 latency <= baseline+30ms). - Automated rollback implemented via feature flag tied to observed metric thresholds. - All runbook steps reviewed and signed off by Eng (runtime), SRE, and Legal (if customer-facing messages required).

Measurement plan: use the Console cost explorer queries + custom Grafana panels. Primary economics metrics: tokens-per-response, net unit-cost delta, GPU utilization uplift. Primary safety metrics: instruction-following score on gold prompts, false-positive rate for safety filters, p95/p99 latency. Secondary metrics: cache hit rate, batched throughput.

Risks & mitigations: - Quantization can introduce subtle regressions: include a small-scale shadow pass (output comparison) and per-request checksum on sampled prompts. - Aggressive batching may increase tail latency: cap batch size for low-traffic routes and add adaptive batch timeout heuristics. - Cache churn could leak stale context: enforce strict TTL and a KV cache invalidation monitor.

Stakeholders: PM: Marina Lopez; Tech lead: Arjun Patel; Runtime eng lead: Priya Menon; SRE: David Kim; Solutions/SE: Leah Ortiz; Legal reviewer: Connor Blake.

Artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EconOps/Field+Healthboard+and+Runbook, Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/eco_ops/healthboard, GitHub feature flag PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12874, Experiment harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/econ-experiments/tree/field-scaffold
